qs.q: In complex multigenic disorders, what percentage of type 1 diabetes risk is contributed by a few HLA alleles?
qs.e: Of the 20 to 30 genes implicated in type 1 diabetes, a few HLA alleles contribute more than 50% of the risk, demonstrating that different polymorphisms vary significantly in their contribution.
qs.s: COMPLEX MULTIGENIC AND CYTOGENETIC DISORDERS - 50 MCQs

qs.q: Which environmental factor is most commonly associated with unmasking the genetic trait in type 2 diabetes mellitus?
qs.e: Type 2 diabetes often first manifests clinically after weight gain, demonstrating how obesity as an environmental factor unmasks the diabetic genetic trait.
qs.s: COMPLEX MULTIGENIC AND CYTOGENETIC DISORDERS - 50 MCQs

qs.q: How many genes are most important among the 20 to 30 genes implicated in type 1 diabetes?
qs.e: Of the 20 to 30 genes implicated in type 1 diabetes, 6 or 7 are considered most important, demonstrating that polymorphisms vary in significance.
qs.s: COMPLEX MULTIGENIC AND CYTOGENETIC DISORDERS - 50 MCQs

qs.q: In Type 1 Diabetes, which HLA haplotypes confer the strongest susceptibility?
qs.e: The HLA-DR3/DQ2 and HLA-DR4/DQ8 haplotypes are most strongly associated with the risk of developing Type 1 DM.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: What is the role of CD8+ T cells in the pathogenesis of Type 1 Diabetes?
o: They cause direct islet cell lysis
qs.e: Type 1 DM is a T-cell-mediated autoimmune disease where CD8+ cytotoxic T cells directly destroy insulin-producing beta cells.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia and fruity-smelling breath is most likely to have which finding that would be LEAST characteristic of untreated type 1 diabetes?
qs.e: The presentation is characteristic of severe insulin deficiency with hyperglycemia, dehydration and possible ketoacidosis. Obesity is not a defining feature of type 1 diabetes, although body weight varies among individuals.

qs.q: In type 1 diabetes, approximately how many genes contribute most significantly to disease risk?
qs.e: While 20-30 genes are implicated in type 1 diabetes, only 6-7 are most important, with a few HLA alleles contributing more than 50% of the risk.

qs.q: Which environmental factor commonly unmasks the genetic trait in type 2 diabetes mellitus?
qs.e: Type 2 diabetes has features of a complex multigenic disorder where obesity and weight gain often unmask the diabetic genetic trait, demonstrating gene-environment interaction.
